subject: Aurea Health — workload map, dedicated sizing & commercial asks
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@aureahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated sizing request — Aurea initial workload snapshot

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to get a clear, line-item recommendation from you for Dedicated (reserved) capacity so we can budget and start an internal procurement timeline. High level we expect to run patient-facing summarization and chart question answering. A few baseline numbers:

- Peak request rate: ~700 requests/minute (spikes up to ~900 for ~10-15m during batch notifications)
- Typical concurrency: 45–60 active sessions during peak
- Avg input tokens per call: 240 tokens (user prompt + context snippets)
- Avg generated tokens per call: 160 tokens
- Working context length: up to 8k tokens for long-chart queries (most calls 1–2k)
- Latency target: p95 < 300 ms for short queries, p99 < 750 ms for long-context queries
- Desired SLA: production availability + maintenance windows; procurement will push for a commercial SLA
- Budget guidance: roughly $150k/month committed if we can get predictable throughput and some burst protection

Can you provide: 1) recommended GPU pool size and configuration, 2) suggested commit term (6/12/24 mo) with indicative pricing, 3) what bursting looks like (limits, overage rates), and 4) any immediate blockers (KV cache sizing / memory constraints) so we can validate with our infra team.

Please include any template we should fill if you need more telemetry.

Thanks —
Erin Walsh
Director, Product Integrations
Aurea Health

[Attachment: aurea_workload_snapshot.xlsx (spreadsheet) — outlined daily/weekly patterns]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@aureahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 13:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — Aurea initial workload snapshot

Erin —

Appreciate the details, that’s a very helpful starting point. I attached a short term-sheet (redwood_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf) and a tiny template you can fill if you want us to run the exact numbers. High-level guidance below — I’ll also loop in our AE and solutions lead to finalize a priced proposal.

Quick recommendation (initial):
- Recommended baseline: 3x H100-class GPUs in a dedicated pod (24/7 reserved).
  - Rationale: with average tokens ~400/request and a peak of ~15 rps, each H100-class GPU supports ~1.2k–1.8k tokens/sec for the model family you ran in the demo with batching. 3 GPUs give ~3.6k–5.4k tokens/sec headroom which covers expected steady-state and allows for concurrency of ~50 with p95 latency targets.
- Burst plan: autoscale to 5 GPUs for short bursts (10–30 minutes) when we see the 10–15m spikes. Bursting billed at reserved blended rate up to a pre-agreed monthly cap; excess bursts billed at on-demand + 25% premium.
- Commit term: 12 months is usually the best balance (we can offer deeper discounts at 24 mo).
- SLA: p99 latency objective will depend on the requested model variant; for your mix we can commit to p95 < 350 ms and p99 < 800 ms on the baseline pool.
- KV caching / RAM note: if you plan many long-context sessions (8k+ tokens often), consider increasing per-GPU memory profile or pinning a small cache tier — this can increase sustained p99.

Indicative commercial (ballpark, subject to final sizing/traffic):
- Baseline 3x reserved GPUs: $145,000/month (list), 12-mo commit discounted to $119,000/month (~18% off)
- Autoscale to 5 GPUs for bursts: included up to 200 GPU-minutes/month; thereafter billed at on-demand hourly rate
- One-time onboarding credit: 2 weeks of free burst capacity for validation

Next steps: if you confirm the traffic pattern in the spreadsheet (I can run a simple simulation), I’ll generate a formal proposed_commit_summary.xlsx and a redlined term sheet.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood_pricing_term_sheet_v1.pdf (PDF) — summary pricing and standard terms]

From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@aureahealth.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing request — Aurea initial workload snapshot

Rafael — thanks, that helps a lot. I filled the spreadsheet with hourly traces for the last 30 days and added a column for heavy-chart windows (see attached). A couple clarifications:

- The heavy window you saw is regular (every weekday at 09:00 local) and lasts ~12–18 minutes with sustained 850–920 req/min.
- We can accept a short ramp (10–14 days) during cutover where latency will be slightly higher. Production SLA needs to be effective after that ramp.
- Procurement wants a capped burst cost model: they’re willing to pay for burst minutes but want a fixed cap per month (we proposed a 15% cap on top of committed spend).

If you can match that cap and include SOC2 + KMS support in the commercial, we can likely push for a 12-month commit. Can you confirm a concrete pricing slide I can bring to procurement?

—Erin

[Attachment: aurea_workload_snapshot.xlsx — updated hourly traces]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@aureahealth.com>

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated sizing request — Aurea initial workload snapshot

Ben / Laura — forwarding Aurea’s filled trace. Key asks: 12-mo commit if we can incorporate a capped burst model (15% additional spend cap) and SOC2 + KMS. Their budget target is ~ $150k/month.

My technical read: baseline 3x H100-class GPUs is defensible for steady-state, but because they have a recurring ~12–18m daily spike up to ~920 req/min we should propose:
- Baseline reserved pool: 3 GPUs (24/7) sized for p95 < 350ms
- Burst pool: can autoscale to 6 GPUs for the 15-minute windows; we recommend we guarantee up to 15% of monthly committed spend for bursting (matches their ask). Excess usage billed at on-demand + 20% premium.
- Ops: include a 14-day ramp window post-cutover where we accept slightly higher p99s while performance tuning KV caching and batch profiles.

Commercial proposal (starter):
- 12-mo commit — $129,500/month (after an 18% discount off list)
- Includes: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration guidance, 2-week onboarding burst credit, and a 15% monthly burst cap at committed pricing.
- If they commit 24-mo: additional 6% discount and guaranteed price protection for model variant swaps (we absorb one model-change migration).

Risks / open items:
- If their heavy-window patterns increase beyond current traces we need to re-trigger capacity planning; recommend a clause that allows a single upsize during the term without penalty.
- We need procurement contact (I ccd them), and a decision on whether they require an on-prem private deployment for regulated PHI paths. That impacts pricing.

Can we take $129.5k/month as a starter counter (12-mo) and offer a 2-month credit for immediate sign? Ben, your thoughts on flexibility here + discount depth.

Rafael
